::: {.callout-important title="Release baseline"}
The repository source is synchronized with the signed `NADABAS.xlam` supplied
for release 6.01.003. The signed `.xlam` and `.xlsm` files remain release
artifacts; they are not committed as editable source files.
:::

## Installation package

Release 6.01.003 is distributed as a ZIP archive containing two signed Office
files:

- `NADABAS.6.01.003.xlsm` is the versioned installer that the user opens;
- `NADABAS.xlam` is the companion Excel add-in and contains the VBA project.

Keep both files together after extraction. Verify the publisher and validity of
both Office signatures before opening the installer. The complete release
manifest, SHA-256 checksums, and installation checklist are recorded in the
[6.01.003 release and installation record](release-6.01.003.qmd).

## Automatic version check

`InterfaceVersionUpdate` schedules a check five seconds after NADABAS starts.
The check is enabled by default and runs at most once every seven days. It sends
a synchronous, read-only HTTPS `GET` request to GitHub's latest-release API and
compares the numeric release tag with `CURRENT_VERSION`, which is `6.01.003` in
this release. `Application.OnTime` delays the request until startup has
completed; it does not make the HTTP request a background operation.

If a newer version exists, NADABAS displays a translated Yes/No message with
the installed and published versions. Selecting Yes opens the familiar
<https://nadabas.net/nadabas/documents-and-downloads> page. NADABAS never
downloads, replaces, or installs a file automatically. Network failures, proxy
restrictions, malformed responses, and current versions are silent during the
automatic check.

The administration menu contains two translated controls:

- **Check for updates** performs a manual check and reports a newer, current,
  or failed result;
- **Check automatically for new NADABAS versions** enables or disables the
  shared policy.

Only a recognized database administrator can change the automatic-check
setting. `UserSettings.CheckForUpdates` stores the database-wide value and
defaults to enabled. The registry values under `NADABAS\VersionUpdate` cache the
last attempted day, last observed public version, and the setting used before a
database has finished loading. Opening a database applies its shared value and
updates the local mirror.

### Publishing the version that NADABAS sees

Publish a non-draft, non-prerelease GitHub release in
`statisticsnorway/nadabas`. Its tag must contain the same numeric value as
`InterfaceVersionUpdate.CURRENT_VERSION`, for example `v6.01.003`. A Git tag
without a published GitHub release is not returned by the latest-release API.

When a pull request from a branch whose name starts with `release_` is merged
into `main`, the release workflow creates a draft release for the version in
`InterfaceVersionUpdate.CURRENT_VERSION`. The workflow pins the draft to the
merged commit, but it does not build, attach, sign, or publish release files.

Attach only reviewed and signed release artifacts. The GitHub release supplies
the public version number, while the user-facing download link remains on
nadabas.net. A maintainer must update and test `CURRENT_VERSION` for every new
release; do not add a test-only latest-version override to production source.

## A downloaded add-in is blocked by Windows

If installation ends with run-time error 53 after a download, close Excel and
locate the extracted `NADABAS.xlam` file. Right-click the file, select
**Properties**, select **Unblock** on the **General** tab, and then select
**Apply** or **OK**. Check the extracted `NADABAS.6.01.003.xlsm` file in the
same way when Windows presents the option. Reopen the versioned installer and
retry.

Release 6.01.003 does not replace VBA's run-time error 53 with localized
unblock instructions, so this recovery procedure must remain available to
users and support staff. Do not unblock a file unless it came from the official
NADABAS download channel and both its Office signature and published checksum
have been verified.

Microsoft documents this behaviour as Mark of the Web and recommends removing
it only for Office files from a trusted source:
<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-apps/security/internet-macros-blocked>.

## Operational safety

Examples must use synthetic values. Credentials, internal endpoints,
production paths, and personal or statistical production data do not belong in
this site. Backup, restore, database conversion, signing, and deployment must
be tested in a non-production environment with a documented rollback path.
